editorial.headline: Computer Retail Is Open Nationally, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers specialist retail sales of computers and related equipment—nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is the specialist retail trade of computers and their equipment. Its scope includes personal computers, laptops, printers, photocopying machines, interactive whiteboards and video-conferencing equipment. The common thread is a retail offer centred on computing hardware and its associated tools: the kind of business that places these products before end customers through a dedicated sales operation. The definition is broad enough to encompass a varied technology assortment, but specific in its commercial focus on computers and the equipment that supports their use.

At national level, the foreign-investment position is clear. The activity is listed as **TERBUKA**, with a maximum foreign ownership allowance of **100%**. In practical terms, a foreign investor may hold the full ownership stake nationally under this activity. The record also makes the activity open across the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the code is not presented as the preserve of one business size: it is available from micro through large-scale enterprise, while retaining the same specialist retail character.

Bali is where the national permission stops being the whole answer. Today, a foreign investor has no route to register this activity as PMA in Bali. The Bali record marks it as blocked on risk-class grounds: at the Besar scale, OSS classifies every scope within the activity as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. That classification brings the activity within Bali’s permanent, province-wide moratorium, recorded here from May 13, 2026. The restriction is therefore not a reduced foreign-ownership percentage or a local ownership condition. It is a bar on PMA registration in Bali for this activity.

The distinction should be read exactly as it stands. Nationally, this is a fully foreign-open specialist computer-retail activity, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling and access across all stated business scales. In Bali, however, the relevant question is no longer how much foreign ownership is permitted. The moratorium prevents PMA registration altogether. For founders considering this activity, that is the decisive geographic fact: the national opening remains real, but it does not create a PMA registration path in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this is fully open to foreign ownership; in Bali, the moratorium prevents PMA registration altogether.
